summary:
The American Football Union (AFU) was a small New York–area league for amateur, semi-professional, and college teams, active from 1886 to 1895. It had little impact on professional football, but its member Orange Athletic Club later became the Orange and Newark Tornadoes, who played in the NFL in 1929 and 1930.

Eight clubs formed the AFU in Manhattan on January 6, 1886. Early membership and schedules were unstable: teams withdrew, disputes arose, and the league’s first season ended with only three teams. Stevens Institute’s Crickets won the inaugural title, going 3–0 in league play.

The Crescent Athletic Club joined in 1887 and dominated for years, winning every title from 1887 through 1892. Orange joined in 1888. In 1890, Orange ended Crescent’s long winning streak against AFU teams, but Crescent beat Orange in the separate championship game. The league adopted stricter membership rules in 1888 and Intercollegiate Football Association rules in 1889; teams continued to withdraw, and Manhattan Athletic Club was admitted in 1890 for the following season.

**Champions:** Stevens Crickets (1886); Crescent (1887–92); Orange (1893–94). The 1895 title is uncertain: the record lists Orange and possibly Crescent.
unsupportedClaims: The AFU adopted stricter membership rules in 1888; the points describe tighter player roster and club-switching rules, not stricter conditions for league membership.
